newsitem.title: USA: Omnicom set to buy Fleishman-Hillard.
newsitem.headline: Omnicom set to buy Fleishman-Hillard.

text.p: Advertising powerhouse Omnicom Group Inc. is expected Wednesday to announce plans to buy public relations firm Fleishman-Hillard Inc. in a transaction valued between $85 and $100 million, according to sources familiar with the situation.
The move would significantly boost Omnicom's growing public relations business which now includes Ketchum and Porter/Novelli.
Spokesmen for New York-based Omnicom and privately-held Fleishman-Hillard declined comment, but a source said the deal would likely be announced late Wednesday afternoon.

Omnicom is one of the world's top advertising agencies, whose holdings include top firms DDB Needham Worldwide and BBDO Worldwide. Some of their biggest clients include Texaco Inc., Montgomery Ward & Co. Inc. and Heinz U.S.A., the largest unit of H.J. Heinz Co.
Speculation about a transaction was reported this week in trade publication Advertising Age, which said the union would create the world's largest public relations company.

The speculation prompted St. Louis, Mo.-based Fleishman-Hillard to issue an internal memo Monday. In the memo, Chairman John Graham declined to comment on the rumored deal, but said any potential transaction involving the public relations firm would aim to broaden the company's growth opportunities.
"In the meantime, the single most important thing for Fleishman-Hillard to do is serve its clients," Graham said in the memo.
For Omnicom, the move would mark the latest in its aggressive acquisition strategy. The company bought Ketchum last year.
"They need it because the advertising and marketing communications business overall doesn't grow as fast as Omnicom wants to grow," said James Dougherty at Dean Witter Reynolds.
It was not immediately known whether the transaction would be for cash or stock, but Dougherty said he would expect it to be accretive to Omnicom earnings.
Shares of Omnicom rose 62.5 cents to $50.125 Tuesday on the New York Stock Exchange.
